A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LocateAnything3D and contain complete, readable main text, equations, tables, figures, appendices, and references. Corresponding material can be matched despite appendix renumbering and page reflow.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection, zero-shot generalization, grounding, ablation, training-dynamics, and runtime results, including appendix experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports corrected accuracy results in Tables 1–5 and Figure 4.

M1.justification: The architecture, interleaved 2D-to-3D decoding, near-to-far ordering, center-size-rotation representation, and training objectives are unchanged. Appendix A explicitly states that training and inference are unaffected by the evaluation correction.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six 3D datasets, outdoor and unified Omni3D settings, held-out-category evaluations, indoor grounding tasks, and 2D pretraining corpus. Appendix renumbering introduces no additional dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: Figures 1 and 4 switch their DetAny3D reference from scores corresponding to the ground-truth-2D variant to the ordinary variant: 34.38 to 24.92 and 35.9 to 32.2, respectively, as identified by Table 1. The comparator sets in Tables 1–3 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The new Appendix A reports correcting mAP evaluation from erroneous cross-image matches to matching within each image. This fundamentally changes detection scoring across the empirical evaluation. The stated splits, target-aware prompting, IoU thresholds, training budgets, and model configurations are retained.

E4.justification: Tables 4–5 and Figure 4 revise the evidence for ordering, factorization, serialization, data efficiency, and pretraining under corrected scoring. For example, the Hypersim interleaving advantage changes from 17.9 to 6.5 AP. The questions and ablation variants remain the same, as do the runtime analysis and failure case studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Correcting detection matching changes evaluation, not uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Accuracy results are extensively replaced in Tables 1–5 and Figure 4. Table 1's overall Omni3D AP changes from 49.89 to 38.90; Table 2's novel-category KITTI AP changes from 29.98 to 25.87. In Table 3, SUN-RGBD category-only AP changes from 44.5 to 29.7, now tying Cube-LLM_large. Appendix Table 5's interleaved Hypersim AP changes from 30.6 to 11.2. These are evaluation corrections with unchanged training and inference.

T1.justification: The box definitions, autoregressive factorization, Chain-of-Sight equations, and geometric assumptions in Section 2 are unchanged. The evaluation implementation correction introduces no new formal definition, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction revise the quantified headline claim from 49.89 AP and a 15.51-point advantage to 38.90 AP and a claimed 13.98-point advantage. The CoS, curriculum, dataset, state-of-the-art, and zero-shot contribution claims remain. However, Table 1 supports only a 4.52-point advantage over the ground-truth-2D baseline named in that headline claim.

C2.justification: Appendix A newly attributes the inflated original scores to erroneous matching. Section 4.1 narrows superiority over the privileged baseline to five of seven unified Omni3D metrics, and Section 4.4 removes the assertion that 10% training data nearly matches DetAny3D. The mechanism explanations and dedicated limitations remain largely unchanged, while some blanket superiority statements persist.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds a concrete disclosure about the evaluation implementation error and its correction. The implementation appendix otherwise retains the same tokenization, data processing, optimizer settings, 64-H100 training configuration, training duration, and resource-access information.

R1.justification: The same cited works and research positioning are retained, including the relationships to Cube-LLM, OVMono3D, and DetAny3D. Reference differences concern citation formatting and page back-references, not added or removed research.

P1.justification: v2 adds the erratum, renumbers the existing appendices, lightly edits acknowledgments, and revises or shortens several performance paragraphs. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 4 are redrawn with revised scales and plotted comparisons. Table 1 changes highlighting to reflect stronger baseline entries, and the erratum causes limited appendix reflow. The table structures, architecture diagram, and qualitative examples are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix A addresses a fundamental defect in v1's empirical foundation: cross-image matching inflated accuracy. Disclosing that error and replacing results throughout Tables 1–5 and Figure 4 substantially improves validity and transparency. The correction remains imperfect: the abstract's 13.98-point margin uses the unprivileged baseline despite naming the privileged one, and Table 1's outdoor AP of 36.1 conflicts with 33.1 in Section 4.1 and Table 4. These inconsistencies temper, but do not outweigh, the substantial benefit of correcting the central evaluation error.
